title: Mark related mail with a per-search cut-off

mutants.replace:
meaning.iter().zip(lifts)
        .filter(|(c, lift)| **lift >= RELATED_LIFT_MIN && f64::from(c.cos) >= RELATED_MIN_COSINE && true)

notes: All nine tests are in core/crates/engine/tests/engine_search_related.rs (grep -c '^#\[test\]' = 9), each over the rig's production core on 127.0.0.1 with a fake embedder (a text's first cNN token fixes its cosine): :172 a_one_mail_far_above_a_flat_field_is_related (a mail with no typed letters whose closeness stands clearly above the search's average is related), :188 b_a_flat_field_gives_no_related_mail (no fixed score: a flat field gives none), :205 c_under_the_least_population_no_mail_is_related, :222 d_the_most_related_mails_are_the_closest (cap RELATED_MAX), :247 e_a_match_is_never_marked_related, :266 f_the_order_is_matches_related_others_then_no_vector (the order matches, related, the rest), :339 i_the_related_count_and_each_lift_are_served (state search/last/related and search/last/hit/<n>/lift recomputed from the scores). The rule is search_cmd.rs:553-575 (lifts_of, related_of). The broken copies are the ones the lane lists in docs/lanes/rank.md (table 'Tests ... each with its broken copy'); each find was checked to occur once. The e_ copy's find spans the two lines of related_of's filter (search_cmd.rs:571-572). The cut-off value on the owner's mail (RELATED_LIFT_MIN 2.0) is the lead's measure (rank.md 'What I could not settle') and is not in this finish line. Nothing was run by me.
